summary: This bill gives the March 6, 2025 executive order establishing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and U.S. Digital Asset Stockpile the full force and effect of law.

scores.thoughts: The bill codifies an executive order establishing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and digital asset stockpile. While this involves government asset management, the legislation itself does not direct new appropriations, mandate purchases, or alter spending levels in any explicit way. It has no bearing on expanding or reducing government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or treatment of digital assets for tax purposes.
No connection to healthcare policy, insurance, public coverage, or market-based healthcare systems.
The bill has no relation to firearms regulation or gun rights.
No provisions addressing immigration pathways, border enforcement, or related protections.
The legislation does not engage with reproductive rights or abortion access.
No impact on military or defense spending levels.
The bill does not address environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
The bill has no bearing on education funding, school choice, or federal involvement in schools.
No engagement with drug decriminalization, enforcement, or related policies.
The legislation does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions on tariffs, free trade agreements, or protectionist measures.
While a Bitcoin reserve could theoretically interact with broader fiscal policy, the bill itself makes no reference to deficits, debt reduction, or deficit spending.
No provisions affecting legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill does not address foreign aid levels or policy.
No relation to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
Although the bill concerns digital assets, it focuses solely on establishing a government stockpile and does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or oversight mechanisms.
No provisions related to worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
